cells.tense: Right now the care in you is letting something grow at its own pace.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Keep tending what you're raising, and this week stop checking whether it worked. Give the care, then turn away from watching. See what it does with the room.
cells.core:
There's something in your care that lets a thing grow at its own speed. You give what's needed, then you leave it alone, and because you don't hover it turns out to be itself rather than the shape you hoped for. That's rare, and it's working here — growth is happening, and your care isn't draining you to make it happen.

The next stretch offers something worth taking. Keep doing the good work, and put the result down. Release isn't losing it — it's what happens when you trust the work is enough. The care stays in your hands. What leaves is the grip.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting it grow by not forcing it.
cells.growth: Release flows naturally from completion — surrender as fulfillment, not defeat
cells.verb: tending what's growing without forcing it
cells.place: where what's already in you comes out and shows

cells.tense: You're bracing for how this turns out, steering it before it's had a chance.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: You're already running the endings in your head for something you're tending. Say one you keep rehearsing aloud, then do the single next thing and stop. No clock on it — go do something else after.
cells.core:
Sometimes the caring gets out in front of the thing being cared for. The whole future gets built in your head — what it'll be, how it'll go, what could still go wrong — and the care starts to feel like steering every turn before the road shows up. Some of what you're carrying was handed to you, not chosen. You get tired, and the thing in your hands gets less room to be itself.

Enough light for the step you're on is the way through. Say the ending you keep rehearsing aloud, then do the single thing that's actually here and stop for now. The road shows itself as you walk, not before you start.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a future you can't see yet.
cells.diagonal: Vision flows from genuine integration — dreaming because experience has been fully processed
cells.verb: tending what's growing without forcing it
cells.place: where what's already in you comes out and shows

cells.tense: Nothing has been growing for a stretch, and you stopped standing near the door.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: There was something you wanted once and quietly set down. Face it again, in your own thinking, and stay with the pull of it. Decide nothing. Just turn toward it.
cells.core:
There's a stretch behind you where nothing wanted to grow, and you arranged your life around making that feel like a choice. The caring is still in you — you feel it nowhere. You stopped turning toward what used to draw you, and staying steady has come to look like being free of wants. It isn't the same thing. You're further from yourself than the door you're at.

What pulls forward doesn't come from effort. It comes from wants — the light you'd steer by if you let yourself. Face a thing you once wanted and stay with the pull of it, to yourself, before you decide anything about it. A direction to face is enough to start.
cells.sheetLine: You're at the door, and it's behind you.
cells.vertical: Radiance flows from genuine development — shining because what was cultivated reached completion
cells.verb: tending what's growing without forcing it
cells.place: where what's already in you comes out and shows

cells.tense: You've been the one people lean on for a long time, and you'd call it just how you are.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: There's upkeep you do for other people that you didn't sign up for. Drop that upkeep for a week — no announcement, no explanation. Leave it and notice what your hands feel like.
cells.core:
Somewhere along the way you became the one who holds things up for others, and by now it feels like your shape rather than a choice. People bring you what they can't carry and you take it, and you talk about it like it's simply how things are. The caring is real — it's why they come. You'd say you're fine. Something in you keeps mentioning that you're tired.

There's a point where holding stops being care and becomes what's left over. Take one piece of upkeep you do for others that you didn't agree to carry, and stop doing it for a week. Don't announce it. Put it down and see what's still in your hands.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in the Too Much draft is that the person's care is 'really' control — the record names boundary dissolution and smothering, not motive; I've written it as what the tending is doing, not why. A reader could reasonably say the offers in Too Little and Unacknowledged ask a depleted person to want and to put something down when nothing is left to give — the acts are the medicine's own, but the person may not have a free hand, so both asks are written as one small move that costs nothing and can be skipped. All four asks survive being wrong: each is a real act of the medicine, useful even if the read misses, and each can be done alone with no money, no energy, no one on hand. The sentence that serves me more than them, cut: 'you were never asked to carry this' — it sounds kind and tells them nothing they can do.
